decisions.what: Shared wire contract authored up front in contract/CONTRACT.md + contract/schemas/, vendored byte-identically into both plugins.
decisions.why: Two independent implementation tracks cannot converge on TreeIR/Diagnostics/Manifest/fingerprint by coincidence. Pinning canonical-JSON rules and the diagnostic path/severity table before any code meant neither side had to guess.

decisions.what: Parallel tracks coordinate through per-track .progress-fragments/*.json merged by tools/merge-progress.py, never by editing a shared PROGRESS.json.
decisions.why: Concurrent writers to one ledger file lose data. The merger also filters each spec's own milestone ids into its own ledger.

decisions.what: Cross-track seams were published as code, not prose: the x_companion_route_{id} filter dispatch on the PHP side, and registerSessionProvider/registerFactoryProvider + a 16-entry registry table on the TypeScript side.
decisions.why: Lets a track ship while its counterpart is unbuilt: routes 501 and tools report not_implemented instead of the package failing to boot. Verified empirically in both directions.

decisions.what: Rewrote 4 assertions in x-agent/tests/validate.test.ts that asserted the six session/oracle/factory tools were NOT implemented.
decisions.why: They encoded build order, not behaviour, and had to fail the moment the work they were waiting for landed. Replaced with the end-state invariant (all 16 declared tools resolve to real handlers) plus a synthetic-placeholder test that keeps covering the not_implemented degradation path, and a note documenting that config resolution precedes the handler for connection-requiring tools.

decisions.what: M1_skeleton, M2_manifest and M7_hardening_and_docs were closed out from live proof-suite and plugin-check evidence gathered by the orchestrator, not by the track that wrote the code.
decisions.why: The core track could only verify against a stubbed WP surface and honestly left them in_progress; M7 spanned two tracks so neither owned it. The acceptance criteria are now met by observed output, which is what the ledger rule actually requires.

deviations.what: M4_harness / M5_block_library / M6_tokens_and_export read 'pending' in x-companion/PROGRESS.json although their implementation files exist and the harness is demonstrably working live.
deviations.why: The track implementing them was terminated by a session limit during its test run, before it wrote its progress fragment. The ledger correctly refuses to claim a milestone without pasted acceptance output. Independent corroboration that the harness works: the session/oracle track compiled fixture trees through GET /harness end to end (cold 1147ms -> warm 5ms), and the docs track drove the same page with Playwright to capture real markup. The library and tokens routes have NOT been independently verified and their tests have not been run.

deviations.what: The acceptance line 'authenticated as x_agent role -> 501' is satisfied as 200, not 501.
deviations.why: 501 described the scaffold-only milestone state, before the routes were implemented. Every route is now implemented, so the meaningful assertion is the auth/tier/posture matrix, which P2 and P11 verify in full.
